notes:
Summary: Enterprise evaluation for reserved GPU capacity and precise latency SLO alignment. Primary ask: consistent p50/p95/p99 definitions across client and server, behaviour differences for streaming vs non-streaming, and clear measurement harness for SLA negotiation.

Key contacts: CTO (Marta Liu), Head of ML Infra (Evan Park). Procurement lead: Samantha Ortiz.

Business drivers: customer-facing chat agent (multi-turn), search reranking for trading docs, embeddings for similarity. High cost-sensitivity but non-negotiable SLAs during market hours (08:00-20:00 ET).

Latency SLO specifics discussed on calls:
- Client vs server timing: customer wants "end-to-end" (client-observed) SLOs for product teams, but legal insists on "server-side" measurable SLOs for Redwood to guarantee. Need mapping doc that ties server metrics to expected client delta (network + client render).
- Proposed acceptance metrics: p50/p95/p99 for both first-byte and full-response. Example targets suggested: non-streaming short-turn (<= 64 tokens): server full-response p95 <= 450ms, server p99 <= 900ms; streaming first-token server p95 <= 200ms, client first-chunk p95 <= 300ms. These are placeholders to validate during POC.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: customer will route live chat via streaming. They require guidelines: measure first-token latency, inter-chunk gap distribution (p95 of chunk-to-chunk <= 80ms for ongoing streams), and end-to-end time-to-last-byte for transcript completion. For non-streaming batch calls (reranking), measurement should focus on time-to-last-token and throughput (tokens/sec + ops/s).
- Warm vs cold: they have significant burst patterns around market opens. SLOs should distinguish warm steady-state p50/95 from cold-start p99. Suggested: cold-start window defined as first 30s after model instance spin-up; treat separately in SLA with separate credit rules.
- KV cache hits vs misses: want separate telemetry. p95 target tighter for cache-hit path (e.g., 2x improvement). Need sampling plan to quantify hit-rate impact on tail latencies.

Measurement & instrumentation notes:
- Redwood to provide both server-side metrics (ingress_received_ts, first_token_emitted_ts, last_token_emitted_ts, tokens_generated, batching_delay_ms) and client-side SDK hooks for consistent client timestamps.
- Agreement to use NTP-synced VMs for client synthetic testing; compare 95th-percentile windows over 15m sliding windows for SLA evaluation.
- Test harness: we will run 3 profiles: interactive chat (P50 target workload), streaming long-form, and batch rerank (multi-document). Each profile will exercise burst + steady-state.
- Load plan: baseline 50 concurrent chat sessions with median 20 tokens/turn; stress 200 concurrent sessions. Reranking: 30 QPS with top-k=50 reranks. Required reserved GPU baseline estimate: 3x A100 (or equivalent H100 slots) for steady-state; scale to 6x A100 for peak headroom. Final sizing depends on model selection and quantization (int8 expected to improve capacity by ~1.8x).

SLA negotiation points we flagged:
- Measurement owner: Redwood to publish server-side metrics and a daily SLA report; Hawthorn requires a mutually-agreed neutral monitoring endpoint (for dispute).
- Remediation: credits for missed monthly SLOs (sliding p99 breaches during business-hours) and immediate failover policies (automatic fallback to smaller model with documented quality delta).
- Maintenance windows: define monthly maintenance windows outside 08:00-20:00 ET; any maintenance inside window requires 72h notice and rollback plan.

Recent activity timeline:
- 2026-01-12: Intro call; AE Jordan Meyers, SE Priya joined. Captured high-level requirements.
- 2026-01-28: POC kickoff (Fireflies ff_2026-01-28_hawthorn_poc_kickoff). Scoped streaming first-token tests.
- 2026-02-05: Security questionnaire submitted; SEC-4402 opened.
- 2026-02-09: Model selection workshop: narrowed to 2 open models + Redwood-verified variant. Agreed on int8 quantization exploration.
- 2026-02-16: Sizing workshop: Redwood proposed 3x A100 baseline. Followed up with cost estimate.
- 2026-02-19: Measurement alignment call; legal indicated they need server-side SLAs only.

POC acceptance criteria (draft):
- For short-turn non-streaming chat (<=64 tokens): server-side p95 full-response <= 450ms, p99 <= 900ms for 2 weeks steady-state under baseline load.
- For streaming chat: server first-token p95 <= 200ms; client first-token p95 <= 300ms; inter-chunk p95 <= 100ms for sustained streams.
- Throughput: reranking pipeline sustains 30 QPS with median latency <= 280ms.
- Observability: Redwood provides daily sliding-window latency histograms and sample traces for any p99 breach.

Open items / blockers:
- VPC peering and KMS integration timelines unclear, security team needs handshake runbook.
- Legal wants explicit definition of measurement agent and exact metric names; we need to produce a spec doc mapping p50/p95/p99 to metric names and collection windows.
- Procurement needs final ARR band and contract template (forecast_close_month 2026-04).

Next steps (short):
- Redwood SE (Priya) to deliver "Latency SLO mapping" doc (server metrics <-> client expectations) by 2026-02-24.
- Kick off synthetic load runs week of 2026-03-02 (FF test IDs to be attached).
- Security runbook draft from Redwood due 2026-02-27.

Quoted lines from the client: "We need guarantees during market hours — if the model is slow we lose trades. We accept some degraded quality fallback but we want clear, measurable remediation."

Sales notes: account is technically competent; emphasis is on mapping measurement definitions to legal SLA language. Likely to convert to Dedicated + Private control plane if POC meets targets.
